html:
Purehno is a name on the map for a group in the forests of northern Pará, Brazil, near the Trombetas and Erepecuru rivers north of the Amazon. Almost nothing is known about it under this name.

This upland is home to Carib-speaking peoples such as the Tiriyó, the Waiwai, the Hixkaryana and the Wayana, who farm manioc and hunt and fish in the forest. Some small groups in the area still avoid contact with outsiders in Brazil.
